landing.explain.title: What Indian equity desks use GCI for
landing.explain.p1: Equity desks already screen news, filings, and price action. Comparing management promises to later reported numbers across quarters still means rebuilding the trail by hand. {product} structures that trail so a Guidance Credibility Index score can be challenged in an IC note and reopened to the original IR deck, transcript, or exchange filing.
landing.explain.p2: GCI scores whether management met, exceeded, missed, dropped, or still has pending quantified guidance — revenue bands, margins, volumes, and capex — against later reported actuals, with primary sources attached. Each citeable point carries period, metric, guided band, actual, outcome label, and a document path so Indian equity desks can defend every row in a guidance-versus-delivery table.
landing.explain.p3: Unlike sentiment dashboards that track tone, the Guidance Credibility Index tracks delivery. Keep sentiment and GCI in separate lines of a memo so narrative never overrides the evidence trail. Coverage begins with Sensex-depth hand-labeled evidence and honest quality badges as the NSE and BSE universe expands.
landing.explain.p4: Guidance is ingested from IR materials and exchange disclosures, extracted with human-in-the-loop review, matched to later actuals for the same metric and period, then rolled into company-level GCI history. Primary filing homes include the National Stock Exchange of India, BSE, and regulatory context from SEBI. {product} does not replace those sources; it indexes delivery against them.

about.what.title: What it is
about.what.p1: CiteAlpha is a product of Ocotillo Innovation Private Limited. It delivers the Guidance Credibility Index (GCI) — a 0–100 score of whether Indian listed-company management delivered on quantified guidance. It is a credit score for promises vs actuals, not a sentiment dashboard and not a price terminal.
about.what.li1: Every citeable score links to period, metric, guided band, actual, label, and source (URL + quote + citation id).
about.what.li2: India beachhead: Sensex-depth hand-labeled evidence first; broader NSE/BSE listings are navigable with honest quality badges.
about.what.li3: Explicit non-goals: no Buy / Hold / Sell, no retail tips, no OMS or live quotes.
about.why.title: Why it is needed
about.why.lede: Desks already have news, filings search, and market terminals. What they still lack is a durable, evidence-linked answer to: did this management keep its word?
about.why.drift.title: Guidance drifts
about.why.drift.text: Bands move mid-year; “dropped” reiterates vanish from memory. Without a thread of statements → actuals, miss patterns stay anecdotal.
about.why.india.title: India-shaped disclosure
about.why.india.text: NSE/BSE IR tables, mixed-language concalls, and local formats need a local spine — not a US-first product with India as an afterthought.
about.why.compliance.title: Compliance posture
about.why.compliance.text: Factual delivery research stays on the right side of SEBI RA risk. Analysts own forecasts; the platform shows observed delivery and citations.
about.why.hitl.title: HITL that compounds
about.why.hitl.text: Extract → review → commit turns desk corrections into a lasting corpus — not a one-off paste into a spreadsheet.
about.how.title: How it works
about.how.lede: One pipeline: ingest → structure → searchable → citable. Citability is not a bolt-on — it only works when documents are stored with structure preserved.
about.pipeline.1.title: Ingest
about.pipeline.1.text: IR pages, transcripts, and filings land in the document store — Sensex crawl first; paste is the exception path.
about.pipeline.2.title: Extract & review
about.pipeline.2.text: Quantified guidance becomes pending statements. Analysts Accept / Edit / Reject before anything enters GCI math.
about.pipeline.3.title: Match & score
about.pipeline.3.text: Guidance bands meet reported actuals. Labels: met, exceeded, missed, dropped, pending — then a 0–100 company GCI.
about.pipeline.4.title: Cite
about.pipeline.4.text: Every citeable score point carries period, metric, quote, URL, and citation id bound to an accepted document.
about.how.note: Data quality stays honest: Hand-labeled for external citation; Provisional listings are scored for screening only — never invent citeable quotes. Analytics overlays (e.g. GCI vs tape) are descriptive patterns, not forecasts. Granger panels show statistical precedence only.
about.layers.title: Capability layers
about.layers.lede: These are product capability layers, not commercial plans. Seats and API access live on Package. Annotated screenshots: tier gallery.
about.layers.foundation.title: Foundation
about.layers.foundation.text: Auto ingest → period docs (transcript / results / IR) → entity search with corpus honesty → citeable citation ids. Desk → Corpus builds the Sensex gate.
about.layers.workflow.title: Workflow
about.layers.workflow.text: Multi-horizon Δ (QoQ/YoY from PIT), GCI↔price descriptive overlays, private notes, role report templates with citation appendix.
about.layers.analytics.title: Analytics (gated)
about.layers.analytics.text: LASSO → Granger F-test and FDR impact map on ≥12-quarter PIT series. Not causation, not a forecast — methodology card on the dossier Analytics panel.
about.layers.oos.title: Out of scope
about.layers.oos.text: Buy/Hold/Sell, treating provisional listing scores as citeable IR evidence, or cloning a global market-intel OS in product chrome.
